domain_label: Structured Analytic Techniques & Knowledge Probes (Knowledge Acquisition subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
these structured analytic techniques are standard intelligence-analysis methods used defensively to improve analytic rigor
an analytic question and at least one knowledge gap statement are available to drive technique selection
the analysis is session-bounded by a decision deadline that constrains how many probes can run
exclusions: collection tasking and source acquisition (delegated to the collection/acquisition layer)
argument mapping and claim-evidence appraisal internals (reused from the argue specialist, not reimplemented)
automated learning of which techniques work best from data
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for structured-analytic-technique probing work units, informed by the standard intelligence-analysis SAT literature; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Heuer 1999 Psychology of Intelligence Analysis (ACH, cognitive bias); Heuer & Pherson 2010/2014 Structured Analytic Techniques for Intelligence Analysis (key assumptions check, what-if, indicators, quality-of-information check, red hat, devil's advocacy); Klein 2007 Performing a Project Premortem (Harvard Business Review); Kahneman 2011 Thinking, Fast and Slow (inside/outside view, anchoring, base-rate neglect); Tetlock & Gardner 2015 Superforecasting (calibration, reference-class forecasting); US Government 2009 A Tradecraft Primer: Structured Analytic Techniques for Improving Intelligence Analysis

competency_questions.question: How are structured analytic techniques selected and composed into a session-bounded probe battery for a given question and gap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TECHNIQUE_SELECT maps question/gap type to techniques; PROBE_BATTERY orders and bounds them

competency_questions.question: How is a competing-hypothesis set generated and structured before evidence is weighed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYPOTHESIS_GEN produces a MECE set including the unlikely hypothesis; DECONFLICT widens it; ACH consumes it

competency_questions.question: How does ACH counter confirmation bias and what role does diagnosticity play?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACH ranks by refutation; DIAGNOSTICITY scores discriminating evidence; BIAS_MITIGATION pairs the counter

competency_questions.question: How is the diagnosticity of evidence scored and used to focus analysis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIAGNOSTICITY rates each item by how strongly it discriminates among hypotheses

competency_questions.question: How are key assumptions surfaced, classified, and tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KAC surfaces and classifies load-bearing assumptions; ASSUMPTION_TEST falsifies them

competency_questions.question: How is each probe's finding tied back to the assumption or gap it was meant to resolve?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSUMPTION_TEST downgrades on failure; PROBE_TO_GAP records the gap status and finding

competency_questions.question: How do what-if and pre-mortem techniques surface blind spots and precursors?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WHATIF back-casts a surprising outcome; PREMORTEM stipulates failure to elicit overlooked failure modes

competency_questions.question: How are divergent scenarios constructed and stress-tested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCENARIO spans key uncertainties with divergent consistent futures; PREMORTEM stresses the judgment

competency_questions.question: How are scenarios and hypotheses converted into observable, falsifiable indicators?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDICATORS pre-specifies observable signposts mapped to SCENARIO and hypotheses

competency_questions.question: How is a high-impact low-probability outcome analyzed without base-rate dismissal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIGH_IMPACT_LOW_PROB examines the tail risk's pathway; INDICATORS warns of probability-raising signs

competency_questions.question: How does the method balance attention between the most-likely case and tail risks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIGH_IMPACT_LOW_PROB frames the tail explicitly while the battery bounds attention by value of information

competency_questions.question: How is the outside view and reference-class base rate brought in, and how are the resulting probabilities calibrated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTSIDE_VIEW anchors on a reference class; CALIBRATION_TRAIN scores confidence against outcomes

competency_questions.question: How is the quality and independence of the evidence base audited, and how does it feed elicitation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QOIC audits provenance and independence; ELICITATION uses vetted evidence in independent judgments

competency_questions.question: How are devil's advocacy and perspective-taking used to break groupthink and mirror-imaging?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEVILS_ADVOCATE builds the opposing case; RED_HAT models the actor's own frame

glossary.definition: a documented, repeatable analytic method that externalizes reasoning to mitigate cognitive bias
a technique applied to a specific gap to elicit a finding, treated as an operator that converts a gap into a recorded result
a mutually exclusive, near-exhaustive set of explanations weighed against all evidence
the degree to which an evidence item discriminates among competing hypotheses
a load-bearing premise whose falsity would overturn the conclusion
a pre-specified observable sign whose appearance warns that a hypothesis or scenario is becoming true
an estimate anchored on a reference-class base rate before case-specific adjustment
apparent corroboration in which multiple sources trace back to a single origin
agreement between stated confidence and observed frequency of being correct
the expected decision-relevant payoff of running a probe, used to order the battery

nodes.definition: Select which structured analytic techniques to deploy as probes, keyed to the analytic question type (explanation, estimate, warning, decision) and the gap type (missing hypothesis, hidden assumption, weak evidence, blind spot).

base.update_signal: taxonomy of question types or gap types is revised

pros.claim: Matching the technique to the question type avoids ritualistic SAT use and spends analyst time where it discriminates
pros.example: a warning question routes to indicators and what-if, not to ACH alone

cons.claim: A rigid selection rubric can mis-route a novel question and exclude a technique that would have helped
cons.example: forcing an estimative question through a diagnostic-only template

failure_modes: technique chosen by habit not by question type
gap type misdiagnosed so the wrong probe is run
acceptance_tests: each selected technique is justified by a stated question type and gap type
revisit_triggers: question-type taxonomy changes
a probe repeatedly yields nothing diagnostic

nodes.definition: Generate a mutually exclusive, collectively near-exhaustive set of competing hypotheses for the question, deliberately including the deception/least-likely hypothesis, before any evidence is weighed.

base.update_signal: hypothesis space proves under-generated for a class of questions

pros.claim: Generating the full competing set first prevents anchoring on the first plausible story and makes ACH possible
pros.example: listing 'coup, election, status quo, external intervention' before weighing any cable

cons.claim: An over-large hypothesis set dilutes diagnosticity and overloads the matrix
cons.example: fifteen near-duplicate hypotheses no evidence can separate

failure_modes: premature convergence to one favored hypothesis
an obvious hypothesis omitted from the set
acceptance_tests: the hypothesis set is mutually exclusive and includes at least one disconfirmable rival
revisit_triggers: a real outcome falls outside the generated set
analysts report the set felt forced

nodes.definition: Run Heuer's Analysis of Competing Hypotheses: build a hypothesis-by-evidence matrix, rate each evidence item's consistency with each hypothesis, and seek to refute rather than confirm, ranking hypotheses by weight of disconfirming evidence.

base.update_signal: ACH matrix structure or refutation logic is revised

pros.claim: Refutation-first ranking counters confirmation bias by promoting the hypothesis with the least disconfirming evidence, not the most supporting
pros.example: the favored hypothesis falls once a single highly inconsistent item is entered

cons.claim: ACH is sensitive to which evidence enters the matrix; selective entry re-imports the bias it aims to remove
cons.example: leaving an inconvenient report out of the matrix

failure_modes: matrix built to confirm a preferred hypothesis
non-diagnostic evidence inflates a hypothesis's apparent support
acceptance_tests: each hypothesis is scored against every evidence item and ranked by disconfirmation
revisit_triggers: new evidence materially changes the matrix
two hypotheses remain inseparable after scoring

nodes.definition: Score the diagnosticity of each evidence item: how strongly it discriminates among the competing hypotheses, so analysis concentrates on the few items that actually move the conclusion rather than on volume.

base.update_signal: diagnosticity rubric or weighting scheme changes

pros.claim: Ranking by diagnosticity focuses effort on the handful of items that separate hypotheses, cutting analyst overload
pros.example: one satellite image that only one hypothesis can survive outweighs ten consistent-with-all reports

cons.claim: Diagnosticity judgments are themselves uncertain; a mis-scored item can over- or under-drive the conclusion
cons.example: treating a deceptive plant as highly diagnostic

failure_modes: volume of consistent evidence mistaken for diagnostic weight
a deceptive item rated as highly diagnostic
acceptance_tests: the most diagnostic evidence items are identified and drive the ranking
revisit_triggers: a key item's diagnosticity is reassessed
deception is suspected for a high-leverage item

nodes.definition: Run the Key Assumptions Check: surface the load-bearing assumptions the current analytic line rests on, classify each as solid, caveated, or unsupported, and flag the ones that would overturn the conclusion if wrong.

base.update_signal: the analytic line or its premises change materially

excluded: testing the assumption empirically (handed to ASSUMPTION_TEST)

pros.claim: Making implicit assumptions explicit converts a hidden single point of failure into an inspectable, testable item
pros.example: surfacing the unstated assumption that a regime's army will stay loyal

cons.claim: Endless assumption-listing can stall analysis without prioritizing which assumptions actually matter
cons.example: cataloguing trivial assumptions while missing the decisive one

failure_modes: the decisive assumption is never surfaced
assumptions listed but none classified by impact
acceptance_tests: every load-bearing assumption is surfaced and classified by how badly it would damage the conclusion if false
revisit_triggers: a new analytic line is adopted
an assumption previously rated solid is challenged

nodes.definition: Test or attempt to falsify each flagged key assumption: identify the observable that would break it, seek that observable, and downgrade or caveat the conclusion when the assumption fails to survive.

base.update_signal: the breaking-observable for an assumption is redefined

pros.claim: Tying each assumption to a breaking observable makes it empirically testable rather than rhetorically asserted
pros.example: 'the army stays loyal' is testable by watching for defections at named garrisons

cons.claim: Some load-bearing assumptions have no near-term observable, so the test cannot resolve them in time
cons.example: an assumption about long-run intent with no near-term signal

failure_modes: assumption assumed true because no test was run
conclusion not downgraded after an assumption broke
acceptance_tests: each load-bearing assumption has a breaking observable and was actively tested, not assumed
revisit_triggers: a breaking observable appears
an untested assumption is found to be decisive

nodes.definition: Run What-If Analysis: assume a surprising but possible outcome has already occurred and reason backward to the pathway that produced it, surfacing precursors and indicators no one is currently tracking.

base.update_signal: the stipulated surprising outcome or its plausibility changes

pros.claim: Assuming the outcome has happened licenses imaginative back-casting that forward estimation suppresses
pros.example: back-casting a sudden currency collapse reveals capital-flight precursors to watch

cons.claim: What-if can manufacture vivid but low-probability pathways that distract from the central estimate
cons.example: an elaborate but far-fetched scenario crowding out the base case

failure_modes: plausible precursors never surfaced
a vivid scenario treated as likely without base-rate grounding
acceptance_tests: at least one trackable precursor is surfaced and converted into an indicator
revisit_triggers: a surfaced precursor is observed
the stipulated outcome is reassessed as implausible

nodes.definition: Run a Pre-Mortem (Klein's prospective hindsight): stipulate that the current judgment has already failed badly, then have the team explain why, surfacing overlooked failure modes and blind spots before commitment.

base.update_signal: the judgment under test or its failure framing changes

excluded: root-cause investigation of a real failure

pros.claim: Prospective hindsight raises the number and candor of identified failure modes versus asking 'what could go wrong'
pros.example: imagining the estimate already wrong elicits the objection no one would raise live

cons.claim: A pre-mortem can devolve into pessimism theater that lists failures without weighting their likelihood
cons.example: brainstorming dozens of failures with no prioritization

failure_modes: failure modes listed but not prioritized
the exercise skipped because the team is confident
acceptance_tests: the team produces and prioritizes overlooked failure modes for the stipulated failure
revisit_triggers: a listed failure mode begins to materialize
the underlying judgment is revised

nodes.definition: Construct a small set of internally consistent, divergent scenarios spanning the key uncertainties, so the estimate is stress-tested across futures rather than pinned to a single most-likely line.

base.update_signal: the driving uncertainties or scenario axes change

pros.claim: Spanning futures with a few divergent scenarios exposes which conclusions are robust and which are scenario-fragile
pros.example: a recommendation that survives all four scenarios is flagged as robust

cons.claim: Too many scenarios or overlapping ones dilute the signal and exhaust the audience
cons.example: eight scenarios that differ only cosmetically

failure_modes: scenarios collapse onto the most-likely line
scenario set omits a plausible divergent future
acceptance_tests: a small set of divergent, internally consistent scenarios spans the key uncertainties
revisit_triggers: a driving uncertainty is resolved
reality tracks outside all scenarios

nodes.definition: Define and monitor indicators (signposts): pre-specified, observable, falsifiable signs whose appearance would signal that a hypothesis or scenario is becoming true, converting blind spots into watched warnings.

base.update_signal: the indicator list or its collection feasibility changes

pros.claim: Pre-specifying indicators before the fact prevents post-hoc rationalization and creates an early-warning tripwire
pros.example: a named troop-movement indicator fires before, not after, the escalation

cons.claim: Indicators that are not actually collectable give false reassurance of vigilance
cons.example: a perfect indicator no sensor can observe

failure_modes: indicators are not observable or collectable
an indicator fires but no one acts on it
acceptance_tests: each indicator is observable, falsifiable, and mapped to the hypothesis or scenario it warns for
revisit_triggers: an indicator fires
an indicator proves uncollectable in practice

nodes.definition: Run High-Impact/Low-Probability analysis: examine a low-likelihood but high-consequence outcome on its own terms, identify the pathway and the indicators that would raise its probability, so it is not dismissed by base rates alone.

base.update_signal: the outcome's consequence assessment or pathway changes

pros.claim: Treating a tail risk on its own terms prevents base-rate neglect of catastrophes that the average case would bury
pros.example: analyzing a low-odds but catastrophic supply-chain rupture explicitly

cons.claim: Over-attending to dramatic low-probability events can skew priorities away from the likely case
cons.example: spending the analysis budget on a vivid but improbable scenario

failure_modes: a catastrophic tail risk dismissed purely on low base rate
tail risk inflated into the central estimate
acceptance_tests: the high-impact low-probability outcome has an explicit pathway and probability-raising indicators
revisit_triggers: a probability-raising indicator appears
the consequence assessment is revised

nodes.definition: Take the outside view: place the case in a reference class and anchor the estimate on the class base rate before adjusting for case specifics, countering the inside-view tendency to over-rely on the vivid particulars of this case.

base.update_signal: the chosen reference class or its base rate changes

pros.claim: Anchoring on a reference-class base rate corrects the inside view's systematic optimism and neglect of base rates
pros.example: forecasting project slippage from the base rate of similar projects, not the team's plan

cons.claim: A poorly chosen or unrepresentative reference class imports its own bias and can mislead more than the inside view
cons.example: using an irrelevant class whose base rate does not apply

failure_modes: base-rate neglect: estimate built only from case particulars
reference class chosen to support a desired number
acceptance_tests: the estimate is anchored on a defensible reference-class base rate before case-specific adjustment
revisit_triggers: a better-fitting reference class is found
the base rate is updated with new class data

nodes.definition: Run a Quality-of-Information Check: audit the provenance, currency, corroboration, and independence of each evidence source, flagging illusory corroboration, single-source dependence, and stale or deceptive material before it drives conclusions.

base.update_signal: the source base or its independence structure changes

pros.claim: Auditing source independence exposes circular reporting where several streams trace to one origin, deflating false corroboration
pros.example: three 'independent' reports that all derive from one informant are collapsed to one

cons.claim: Aggressive sourcing scrutiny can discard genuinely useful but imperfectly provenanced evidence
cons.example: rejecting a timely report because its chain is not fully documented

failure_modes: illusory corroboration from circular reporting
stale or deceptive source treated as current and reliable
acceptance_tests: every evidence item carries a provenance, currency, and independence rating before it is weighed
revisit_triggers: a source is found to be circular or deceptive
new sourcing changes an item's reliability

nodes.definition: Assign a devil's advocate / red team to build the strongest case against the prevailing analytic line, stress-testing it for groupthink and surfacing the disconfirming evidence the consensus has discounted.

base.update_signal: the prevailing analytic line or team composition changes

pros.claim: A standing devil's advocate institutionalizes dissent, breaking the consensus that suppresses inconvenient evidence
pros.example: the red cell forces the team to confront the report it had explained away

cons.claim: Routine or token devil's advocacy breeds cynicism and can corrode team cohesion if it never changes outcomes
cons.example: an advocate whose objections are ritually overruled

failure_modes: dissent suppressed by group pressure
devil's advocacy is ritual and never affects the conclusion
acceptance_tests: the strongest opposing case is built and explicitly adjudicated, not dismissed
revisit_triggers: consensus forms with no recorded dissent
the opposing case materially weakens the mainline

nodes.definition: Run Red Hat analysis: model the decision from the adversary's or another actor's frame of reference and incentives, rather than mirror-imaging one's own logic onto them, to surface choices the home frame would not predict.

base.update_signal: the modeled actor's incentives or culture are reassessed

pros.claim: Adopting the actor's own frame counters mirror-imaging and predicts choices that look irrational only from the home frame
pros.example: modeling an adversary who values regime survival over economic rationality

cons.claim: Role-play can substitute caricature for genuine understanding of the actor's frame
cons.example: a cartoonish stand-in that confirms existing expectations

failure_modes: mirror-imaging: own logic projected onto the actor
caricature mistaken for the actor's real frame
acceptance_tests: the actor's likely choice is derived from their own incentives and frame, not the analyst's
revisit_triggers: new evidence about the actor's incentives appears
a predicted choice is contradicted by behavior

nodes.definition: Run structured brainstorming and deconfliction: diverge to surface the widest set of ideas and hypotheses without premature criticism, then converge by clustering, deduplicating, and resolving contradictions across analysts.

base.update_signal: the divergence/convergence protocol changes

pros.claim: Separating silent divergence from convergence prevents early anchoring and dominant-voice capture in group ideation
pros.example: round-robin silent generation before discussion surfaces minority hypotheses

cons.claim: Poorly facilitated brainstorming reverts to anchoring on the first or loudest idea
cons.example: the senior analyst's opinion framing the whole session

failure_modes: dominant voice anchors the group early
contradictions left unresolved across analysts
acceptance_tests: divergence is silent and unjudged before convergence clusters and deconflicts the ideas
revisit_triggers: a new analyst joins the cell
contradictory hypotheses persist after convergence

nodes.definition: Apply targeted cognitive-bias mitigation: name the biases most likely in this question (confirmation, anchoring, availability, base-rate neglect) and pair each with the specific technique or check that counters it, so debiasing is mechanism-specific not generic.

base.update_signal: the bias inventory or the technique-to-bias mapping changes

pros.claim: Pairing each likely bias with the specific counter-technique makes debiasing mechanism-specific instead of an unfalsifiable claim
pros.example: confirmation bias countered by ACH refutation; base-rate neglect by the outside view

cons.claim: Bias-awareness alone does not remove bias and can produce overconfidence that debiasing has succeeded
cons.example: a team that believes naming a bias has neutralized it

failure_modes: debiasing claimed without any specific mechanism
awareness mistaken for mitigation
acceptance_tests: each material bias is named and paired with the concrete technique or check that counters it
revisit_triggers: a new bias is implicated by an error review
a counter-technique proves ineffective

nodes.definition: Run a structured expert-elicitation protocol: frame unambiguous questions, elicit independent judgments before discussion to avoid herding, decompose complex quantities, and document rationales, converting a knowledge gap into a defensible aggregated judgment.

base.update_signal: the elicitation protocol or expert panel changes

pros.claim: Eliciting independent judgments before discussion prevents anchoring and herding on a dominant expert
pros.example: each expert records an estimate privately before the panel talks

cons.claim: Aggregating poorly calibrated or correlated experts can produce confident but wrong consensus
cons.example: five experts who all read the same flawed report

failure_modes: herding on the first or most senior expert
correlated experts mistaken for independent confirmation
acceptance_tests: judgments are elicited independently before discussion and each carries a documented rationale
revisit_triggers: the expert panel changes
experts are found to share a common source

nodes.definition: Calibrate probability judgments: train and score analysts so stated confidence matches observed hit rates, use clear probability vocabulary, and track Brier scores so the elicited probabilities are trustworthy, not merely confident.

base.update_signal: the calibration scoring scheme or probability lexicon changes

pros.claim: Calibration training measurably narrows the gap between stated confidence and actual hit rate over repeated forecasts
pros.example: tracked Brier scores improve as analysts learn to widen overconfident intervals

cons.claim: Calibration needs repeated, resolvable forecasts and timely feedback, which many one-off analytic questions never get
cons.example: a unique geopolitical event that never recurs for scoring

failure_modes: overconfidence: stated probabilities exceed observed hit rates
vague verbal probabilities with no numeric anchor
acceptance_tests: stated probabilities are scored against outcomes and the calibration gap is tracked over time
revisit_triggers: a batch of forecasts resolves
systematic over- or under-confidence is detected

nodes.definition: Map each probe to the specific knowledge gap it addresses: record, per gap, which technique was run, what it elicited, and whether the gap is now closed, narrowed, or confirmed as a residual unknown, producing a gap-by-probe traceability record.

base.update_signal: the gap taxonomy or the probe-to-gap mapping changes

pros.claim: A gap-by-probe record makes coverage auditable: every identified gap shows which probe addressed it and what changed
pros.example: a gap table where each row names the gap, the probe, and the residual uncertainty

cons.claim: Forcing every gap onto a probe can give false closure when the probe only partially addressed it
cons.example: marking a gap closed because a probe ran, not because it resolved

failure_modes: a knowledge gap left with no probe assigned
a gap marked closed without an elicited finding to justify it
acceptance_tests: every identified knowledge gap maps to at least one probe and a recorded status and finding
revisit_triggers: a new knowledge gap is identified
a probe's finding is overturned by later evidence

nodes.definition: Compose the probe battery for a question: sequence and bound the selected techniques into a session-scoped plan ordered by value of information, so the most decision-relevant probes run first within the analysis deadline.

base.update_signal: the value-of-information ranking or the session time budget changes

excluded: running individual probes (delegated to each technique node)

pros.claim: Ordering the battery by value of information delivers the most decision-relevant findings before the deadline forces a stop
pros.example: running the diagnosticity-cutting probe before lower-value checks when time is short

cons.claim: A maximal battery can overrun the decision deadline and dilute focus across low-value probes
cons.example: running all techniques on every question regardless of payoff

failure_modes: battery overruns the decision deadline
low-value probes crowd out the decisive one
acceptance_tests: the battery is ordered by value of information and bounded to fit the analysis deadline
revisit_triggers: the decision deadline changes
a probe's realized value differs sharply from its expected value

edges.why_related: diagnosticity weighting must be discounted by QOIC source-quality and independence ratings
residual gaps after probing feed back to re-select techniques for the next pass
calibration scores feed back to temper the confidence ACH rankings are reported with
a broken key assumption forces re-rating of the ACH matrix it supported
the adversary frame surfaces hypotheses to add back into the competing set
resolved indicators provide the outcomes that calibrate probability judgments
the opposing case surfaces discounted evidence whose diagnosticity must be re-scored
bias counters constrain how expert judgments are elicited and aggregated

edges.resolution_rule: bound the battery by the decision deadline: when full SAT rigor cannot complete in time, run only the highest value-of-information probes and record the un-run techniques as accepted residual risk
edges.why_related: technique rigor and time-cost conflict with the decision deadline that bounds the analysis session
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: cap the ACH matrix at the most diagnostic evidence: when the full matrix overloads analysts, restrict scoring to high-diagnosticity items and explicitly note the truncation rather than abandoning ACH
edges.why_related: exhaustive ACH diagnosticity scoring conflicts with analyst overload and the cost of a large matrix
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: institutionalize dissent without corroding cohesion: rotate the devil's-advocate role and require the team to adjudicate the opposing case on the record, so challenge is structural rather than personal
edges.why_related: devil's advocacy needed against groupthink conflicts with team cohesion and consensus-building
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: order probes by value of information and stop at diminishing returns: run additional probes only while their expected gap-resolution exceeds their cost, rather than mapping every gap to a probe
edges.why_related: running many probes for full gap coverage conflicts with focused value-of-information and a stop rule
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: technique_rigor_vs_decision_deadline
conflict_axes.description: Full SAT rigor improves quality but the time cost can miss the decision deadline that bounds the session.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: order probes by value of information and stop at the deadline, recording un-run techniques as residual risk

conflict_axes.name: ach_diagnosticity_vs_analyst_overload
conflict_axes.description: Scoring every evidence item against every hypothesis is thorough but can overload analysts and dilute focus.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restrict the matrix to high-diagnosticity items and note the truncation

conflict_axes.name: devils_advocacy_vs_team_cohesion
conflict_axes.description: Institutionalized dissent breaks groupthink but routine adversarial challenge can corrode team cohesion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rotate the role and adjudicate the opposing case on the record

conflict_axes.name: probe_coverage_vs_value_of_information
conflict_axes.description: Mapping every gap to a probe maximizes coverage but can run low-value probes past the point of diminishing returns.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: order by value of information and stop when expected resolution falls below cost

conflict_axes.name: inside_view_vs_outside_view
conflict_axes.description: Case-specific detail captures particulars but neglects base rates; the outside view anchors on base rates but can ignore genuine specifics.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: anchor on the reference-class base rate, then adjust for case specifics under a cap

conflict_axes.name: hypothesis_breadth_vs_matrix_tractability
conflict_axes.description: A wide hypothesis set reduces the chance of omission but a large set dilutes diagnosticity and overloads the ACH matrix.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: generate broadly, then deconflict to a MECE set that keeps the disconfirmable rival

conflict_axes.name: source_scrutiny_vs_timeliness
conflict_axes.description: Deep quality-of-information vetting deflates illusory corroboration but can discard timely evidence whose provenance is imperfect.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: rate provenance and independence, caveat rather than discard timely but thin sources

conflict_axes.name: expert_independence_vs_shared_understanding
conflict_axes.description: Independent elicitation prevents herding but experts then lack the shared context that discussion provides.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: elicit independently first, then share and allow documented revision

conflict_axes.name: tail_risk_attention_vs_central_estimate
conflict_axes.description: Explicit high-impact low-probability analysis avoids base-rate neglect but over-attending to the tail can skew priorities from the likely case.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: analyze the tail on its own terms but weight battery attention by value of information

edge_cases.description: All probes confirm the favored hypothesis because inconvenient evidence was never entered into the ACH matrix.
edge_cases.trigger: selective evidence entry re-imports confirmation bias
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce refutation-first scoring and require every collected item be entered or explicitly excluded with reason

edge_cases.description: A decisive load-bearing assumption is never surfaced, so a confident conclusion rests on an untested premise.
edge_cases.trigger: key assumptions check omits the decisive assumption
edge_cases.mitigation: classify assumptions by impact and require a breaking observable for each load-bearing one

edge_cases.description: Several 'independent' reports turn out to trace to one source, inflating false corroboration.
edge_cases.trigger: circular reporting not detected by the quality-of-information check
edge_cases.mitigation: audit source independence and collapse circular streams to a single origin

edge_cases.description: A catastrophic tail risk is dismissed purely on its low base rate and never analyzed.
edge_cases.trigger: base-rate neglect in reverse: low probability used to skip analysis
edge_cases.mitigation: analyze high-consequence outcomes on their own terms with probability-raising indicators

edge_cases.description: The probe battery overruns the decision deadline and the decision is made before the decisive probe completes.
edge_cases.trigger: battery not ordered by value of information or not time-bounded
edge_cases.mitigation: order probes by value of information and bound the session; record un-run techniques as residual risk

edge_cases.description: Devil's advocacy becomes ritual: objections are raised and overruled without affecting any conclusion, breeding cynicism.
edge_cases.trigger: adversarial challenge never adjudicated on the record
edge_cases.mitigation: require explicit on-record adjudication of the opposing case and rotate the role

edge_cases.description: Mirror-imaging: the actor's likely choice is predicted from the analyst's own logic, missing a frame-specific decision.
edge_cases.trigger: red-hat analysis projects home-frame rationality onto the actor
edge_cases.mitigation: derive the actor's choice from their own incentives and culture, not the analyst's

edge_cases.description: Stated probabilities are systematically overconfident because analysts are never scored against outcomes.
edge_cases.trigger: no calibration feedback loop on resolved forecasts
edge_cases.mitigation: track Brier scores on resolvable forecasts and widen overconfident intervals

edge_cases.description: Indicators are defined but not actually collectable, giving false reassurance of early warning.
edge_cases.trigger: indicator specified without an observability/collection check
edge_cases.mitigation: require each indicator to pass an observability and collection-feasibility check

edge_cases.description: Experts herd on the most senior voice because judgments were shared before being recorded independently.
edge_cases.mitigation: record private judgments before any discussion, then allow documented revision

edge_cases.description: A pre-mortem lists many failure modes but none are prioritized, so the decisive one is buried.
edge_cases.trigger: prospective hindsight produces an unranked failure list
edge_cases.mitigation: rank elicited failure modes by plausibility and impact before reporting

edge_cases.description: A knowledge gap is marked closed because a probe ran, even though the probe only partially addressed it.
edge_cases.mitigation: record gap status as closed/narrowed/residual with the elicited finding that justifies it

workflow.description: Classify the question and gap types and select the structured techniques whose probes address them.
workflow.gate: each selected technique is justified by a stated question and gap type

workflow.description: Generate a MECE competing-hypothesis set including the unlikely/deception hypothesis.
workflow.gate: set is mutually exclusive and includes a disconfirmable rival

workflow.description: Build the hypothesis-evidence matrix and rank by refutation, not confirmation.
workflow.gate: every hypothesis scored against every entered evidence item

workflow.description: Rate each evidence item's discriminating power and flag non-diagnostic items.
workflow.gate: the most diagnostic items are identified and drive the ranking

workflow.description: Surface and classify load-bearing assumptions by impact if false.
workflow.gate: each load-bearing assumption is surfaced and impact-classified

workflow.description: Define each assumption's breaking observable and attempt falsification; downgrade on failure.
workflow.gate: each load-bearing assumption has a breaking observable and was tested

workflow.description: Run what-if and pre-mortem probes to back-cast surprises and elicit overlooked failure modes.
workflow.gate: at least one trackable precursor or prioritized failure mode is surfaced

workflow.description: Construct divergent scenarios and pre-specify observable, falsifiable indicators mapped to them.
workflow.gate: each indicator is observable, falsifiable, and mapped to a hypothesis or scenario

workflow.description: Audit provenance, currency, and independence; flag circular reporting and deception.
workflow.gate: every evidence item carries a provenance and independence rating

workflow.description: Run devil's advocacy and red-hat challenge; anchor on the outside view and calibrate probabilities.
workflow.gate: the opposing case is adjudicated on the record and probabilities are calibrated

workflow.description: Record, per gap, which probe ran, what it elicited, and the gap status.
workflow.gate: every identified gap maps to a probe, a finding, and a status

workflow.description: Order the probes by value of information and bound the battery to the decision deadline.
workflow.gate: battery ordered by value of information and bounded to the deadline

dominance_rules.rule: TECHNIQUE_SELECT must justify each probe by question and gap type before any probe runs
dominance_rules.rationale: ritualistic SAT use wastes analyst time and misroutes gaps
dominance_rules.trigger: a probe is queued without a stated question/gap justification
dominance_rules.action: block the probe until its question and gap type are recorded

dominance_rules.rule: HYPOTHESIS_GEN must produce a MECE set with at least one disconfirmable rival before ACH runs
dominance_rules.rationale: ACH on an anchored or incomplete set re-imports the bias it counters
dominance_rules.trigger: the matrix is built on a single working hypothesis
dominance_rules.action: return to hypothesis generation and deconfliction

dominance_rules.rule: ACH must rank by disconfirming evidence, never by count of supporting evidence
dominance_rules.rationale: refutation-first ranking is what counters confirmation bias
dominance_rules.trigger: a hypothesis ranked by supporting-evidence count
dominance_rules.action: re-rank by weight of inconsistent evidence

dominance_rules.rule: DIAGNOSTICITY weighting must be discounted by QOIC source-quality before driving the ranking
dominance_rules.rationale: a deceptive or circular source rated diagnostic corrupts the conclusion
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-diagnosticity item with an unverified or circular source
dominance_rules.action: discount its weight pending source validation

dominance_rules.rule: Each load-bearing assumption from KAC must have a breaking observable in ASSUMPTION_TEST before the conclusion is finalized
dominance_rules.rationale: an untested decisive assumption is a hidden single point of failure
dominance_rules.trigger: a load-bearing assumption with no breaking observable
dominance_rules.action: define the observable or caveat the conclusion

dominance_rules.rule: DEVILS_ADVOCATE must adjudicate the opposing case on the record before consensus is declared
dominance_rules.rationale: unadjudicated dissent leaves groupthink intact and breeds cynicism
dominance_rules.trigger: consensus declared with no recorded adjudication
dominance_rules.action: require explicit on-record adjudication and rotate the role

dominance_rules.rule: OUTSIDE_VIEW base rate must be set before inside-view case adjustment in any probability estimate
dominance_rules.rationale: starting from case particulars produces base-rate neglect
dominance_rules.trigger: an estimate built only from case-specific detail
dominance_rules.action: anchor on a defensible reference class first

dominance_rules.rule: PROBE_TO_GAP must record a status and elicited finding for every gap before PROBE_BATTERY closes
dominance_rules.rationale: a gap marked closed without a finding is false closure
dominance_rules.trigger: a gap closed with no elicited finding
dominance_rules.action: record closed/narrowed/residual with the justifying finding

dominance_rules.rule: PROBE_BATTERY must be ordered by value of information and bounded to the decision deadline
dominance_rules.rationale: an unbounded battery misses the deadline and dilutes focus
dominance_rules.trigger: a battery that cannot complete before the deadline
dominance_rules.action: run highest-VOI probes first and record un-run techniques as residual risk

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run probes before classifying the question and gap; mis-routed probes are wasted effort
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running a probe battery after discovering the gap type was misdiagnosed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not build the ACH matrix before the hypothesis set is MECE and deconflicted
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the matrix after a missing hypothesis is added late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not let diagnosticity scores drive the ranking before source quality is checked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-scoring the matrix after a high-diagnosticity item is found circular or deceptive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize a conclusion before key assumptions have breaking observables and were tested
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reopening the conclusion when an untested decisive assumption later breaks

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not declare consensus before the opposing case is adjudicated on the record
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking the estimate after late dissent surfaces discounted evidence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not estimate probabilities from case particulars before anchoring on a base rate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deriving an estimate after base-rate neglect is caught in review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not mark a gap closed without recording the elicited finding that justifies it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-probing a gap that was falsely marked closed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not enlarge the battery past the deadline without a value-of-information stop rule
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-planning the session after low-value probes consume the time budget

iteration_protocol.trigger: every probe confirms the favored hypothesis
iteration_protocol.action: audit ACH evidence entry and re-run DIAGNOSTICITY with BIAS_MITIGATION counters for confirmation bias

iteration_protocol.trigger: a load-bearing assumption is found untested and decisive
iteration_protocol.action: return to KAC and define a breaking observable in ASSUMPTION_TEST before finalizing

iteration_protocol.trigger: circular reporting or a deceptive source is discovered
iteration_protocol.action: re-run QOIC and re-score affected items in DIAGNOSTICITY
re-order PROBE_BATTERY by value of information and record un-run techniques in PROBE_TO_GAP as residual risk

iteration_protocol.trigger: a calibration batch shows systematic overconfidence
iteration_protocol.action: re-run CALIBRATION_TRAIN feedback and re-anchor estimates on OUTSIDE_VIEW base rates

iteration_protocol.trigger: consensus formed with no recorded dissent
iteration_protocol.action: re-run DEVILS_ADVOCATE and RED_HAT and adjudicate the opposing case on the record

iteration_protocol.trigger: an indicator proves uncollectable in practice
iteration_protocol.action: revise INDICATORS for observability and re-link to the scenario it warns for

priority_rationale: TECHNIQUE_SELECT and HYPOTHESIS_GEN are foundational; ACH/DIAGNOSTICITY, KAC/ASSUMPTION_TEST, and the imaginative and calibration probes are the core techniques; challenge and bias-mitigation harden them; PROBE_TO_GAP and PROBE_BATTERY synthesize coverage and ordering last.
